title: She didn't tell (Esther 2)
hook: Esther keeps her people and her kindred to herself at the palace

segments.voice: Yesterday, Queen Vashti refused to be put on display, and lost her place. Your line was vashti said no. Whose no did you respect? Today, the empty seat is filled, by a young woman with a secret. Day eight hundred sixty-five.

She has two names. The book introduces her as Hadassah, that is, Esther. She has neither father nor mother. Her cousin Mordecai, the text says, took her for his own daughter. Then the king's officers gather young women from across the empire to the palace, and she is taken too. And at that moment the book stops to tell us about something she doesn't say. Today's word is her silence.
screen: `HADASSAH, THAT IS, ESTHER.` → `RAISED BY HER COUSIN MORDECAI.` → `SOMETHING SHE DOESN'T SAY.`

segments.voice: She didn't tell. In the JPS 1917 translation: "Esther had not made known her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not tell it." She's in the house of the women, in the care of the king's chamberlain Hegai, and nobody there knows she's a Jew. The text doesn't say why Mordecai asked this of her. It lets you feel the danger without naming it. Then comes a small detail that's easy to miss. Every day, Mordecai walks in front of the court of the women's house, to know how Esther did, and what would become of her. The text doesn't say he goes in. He walks past, every day, just to know how she is. When her turn comes to go to the king, she asks for nothing beyond what Hegai advises. The king loves her above all the women and sets the royal crown on her head. A great feast is held, Esther's feast. And then the book says it again, almost word for word: "Esther had not yet made known her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her." Now she's queen, and still she hasn't told. The repetition is the point. The crown didn't change the secret. She keeps it in the women's house, and she keeps it on the throne. In this story the silence reads less like shame than like waiting: one true thing held close until the day it's needed. The book doesn't say yet when that day will come. For now: she didn't tell. Not yet.
screen: `SHE HAD NOT MADE KNOWN HER PEOPLE.` · `MORDECAI WALKS PAST EVERY DAY.` · then, large: `CROWNED, AND STILL SHE HASN'T TOLD.` · then: `ONE TRUE THING, KEPT CLOSE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice what you keep hidden. Ask yourself, gently: what part of who I am do I keep quiet in certain rooms? A belief, a background, a language, a grief, a hope. You don't have to decide whether keeping it quiet is wise. Just notice it, and notice where you keep it. Then think of one place, or one person, where it would be safe to be seen. If you pray, you can bring what's hidden there too. The bell holds the time.
Hadassah. Esther's other name: she keeps her people and her kindred to herself, even after the crown. Today's word.
Your line: one true thing held close. Today, notice one thing you're holding back, and one person you might trust with it someday. Day eight hundred sixty-five.

howItsDone: On Purim the scroll of Esther is chanted in synagogue, and the custom of dressing in costume is linked by some to the way Esther's identity stays hidden in the story.
